propositions: A transient git fetch hang on the GitHub mirror times out after 300s and is converted to SnapshotFetchError, which the adapter blanket-catches and maps to a spurious LLM-Review -1 vote
The spurious -1 vote removes the change from backfill reconciliation's re-pick pool because reconcile.py filters out changes that already have LLM-Review votes
Network stalls are structurally guaranteed to fire the inner _GIT_TIMEOUT (300s) before the outer REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (1200s), ensuring the vote-bearing path is taken

Retryable infrastructure faults (git fetch timeout, connection error) should abstain without voting so changes remain eligible for backfill retry, matching the no-vote safety path already implemented in app.py and reconcile.py

The fix distinguishes retryable infrastructure exceptions (SnapshotFetchError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) from genuine review conclusions and returns ABSTAIN instead of BLOCK
An abstained vote posts no Gerrit vote, writes no dedup row, and emits a VOTER_ERROR marker so the fault is observable but the change remains vote-less and re-drivable by backfill
